episode.title: Redact secrets at terminal exception-result and ACP stderr boundaries
episode.before: At parent commit 2a743e5f4377419c54054ce7c65c79cff98a092c, terminal_tool serialized raw exception text and traceback.format_exc() into model-visible JSON for both the generic exception handler and the TERMINAL_DEGRADED_MODE=fail branch. ACP logging setup also replaced root handlers with a stderr handler using plain logging.Formatter, so that independently configured diagnostic surface bypassed the repository's redacting formatter.
episode.after: At commit 72eda946be949a5932923df3325037a0d6c5da49, both terminal error-result branches apply redact_sensitive_text to the error and traceback fields before JSON serialization, preserving the structured failure response while masking secrets. ACP stderr setup uses RedactingFormatter, causing formatted log records on that handler to pass through the shared secret-redaction policy.
episode.diff: The implementation changes two diagnostic emission boundaries without changing the redaction algorithm: tools/terminal_tool.py adds lazy imports of redact_sensitive_text and sanitizes four outgoing field values across two exception paths; acp_adapter/entry.py replaces logging.Formatter with RedactingFormatter. Two regression-test modules add three tests that inject prefixed secrets and assert that secret values are absent while useful context and response structure remain. The commit reports 98 insertions and 5 deletions across four files.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 72eda946be949a5932923df3325037a0d6c5da49 is an implementation-bearing security fix for issue/PR 77484, with parent 2a743e5f4377419c54054ce7c65c79cff98a092c and four changed files.
In the parent state, both the degraded-fail EnvironmentConnectionError branch and the generic exception branch returned raw str(e) in error and raw traceback.format_exc() in traceback.
evidence_units.source: git show 2a743e5f4377419c54054ce7c65c79cff98a092c:tools/terminal_tool.py, terminal_tool exception handlers around lines 3300-3348

evidence_units.claim: The pinned change applies redact_sensitive_text separately to the model-visible error and traceback fields in both terminal exception-result branches before json.dumps.
terminal_tool returns these dictionaries as JSON tool results, making their error and traceback fields a model-facing diagnostic boundary rather than merely internal logger output.
evidence_units.source: git show 72eda946be949a5932923df3325037a0d6c5da49:tools/terminal_tool.py, returns in EnvironmentConnectionError degraded_mode == 'fail' and except Exception handlers

evidence_units.claim: In the parent state, _setup_logging created a stderr StreamHandler, assigned a plain logging.Formatter, cleared the root handlers, and installed that handler, bypassing formatter-level redaction for ACP stderr.

The pinned change imports RedactingFormatter and uses it in place of logging.Formatter while retaining the existing stderr destination, format string, filter, root-handler replacement, and logging levels.

The shared redact_sensitive_text function passes nonmatching text through, is enabled by default, and masks recognized secrets; RedactingFormatter formats a record normally and then applies redact_sensitive_text to the complete formatted string.

The generic-exception regression test forces _get_env_config to raise an exception containing a prefixed secret and asserts error status, absence of the secret from both error and traceback, and preservation of the key label and failure context.

The degraded-fail regression test enables TERMINAL_DEGRADED_MODE=fail, injects an EnvironmentConnectionError containing a prefixed secret, and asserts that neither returned error nor traceback contains the secret.

The ACP regression test invokes _setup_logging, formats a LogRecord containing an API-key assignment through the installed root handler, and asserts that the secret is absent while the key label remains.
git diff --check reports no whitespace errors for the parent-to-pinned change.

The focused tests could not be executed in the supplied environment because python is absent and python3 does not have pytest installed; therefore runtime pass status was not independently established during extraction.
evidence_units.source: local commands: python -m pytest returned 'python: command not found'; python3 -m pytest returned 'No module named pytest'

candidate_atomics.name: redact-structured-exception-diagnostics-before-return
candidate_atomics.title: Redact exception diagnostics before returning them to the caller
candidate_atomics.description: Sanitize exception-derived message and traceback fields at a structured result boundary while retaining status, field structure, and non-secret diagnostic context.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent credentials embedded in exceptions or failing command context from reaching a diagnostic-result consumer without removing the actionable failure response.
semantic_action.pre_state: An exception handler is about to serialize exception-derived text and traceback content into an externally consumed error result, and those strings may contain secret assignments or prefixed credentials.
semantic_action.post_state: Every exception-derived text field on the affected error-result branches has passed through the shared sensitive-text redactor before serialization; response status, schema, and non-secret context remain available.
semantic_action.validation: Force each affected exception branch with a recognizable secret in the exception text, parse the returned result, assert the error status and expected fields, assert the raw secret is absent from every diagnostic field, and assert useful labels or failure context remain.
parameters: outgoing diagnostic fields: error and traceback
affected branches: generic exception and configured degraded-fail exception

candidate_atomics.name: install-redacting-formatter-on-isolated-log-sink
candidate_atomics.title: Install redaction on an independently configured diagnostic log sink
candidate_atomics.description: Use the shared redacting formatter when a subsystem replaces global logging handlers with its own stderr handler, preserving existing routing and filtering behavior.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent an independently configured log sink from bypassing the application's secret-redaction policy.
semantic_action.pre_state: A subsystem clears inherited root handlers and installs its own diagnostic handler with a plain formatter, so records emitted through that handler are not redacted.
semantic_action.post_state: The subsystem-owned handler formats complete log records through the shared redacting formatter while retaining its destination, layout, filters, and logging-level behavior.
semantic_action.validation: Run the logging setup, obtain the installed handler, format a record containing a recognizable secret assignment, assert the raw secret is absent, and assert the non-secret key label remains.

candidate_workflows.name: close-secret-leaks-across-diagnostic-emission-boundaries
candidate_workflows.title: Close secret leaks at structured-result and log-output boundaries
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for applying an existing redaction policy to diagnostic surfaces that bypass it: sanitize exception-derived fields immediately before structured return, and attach the shared formatter to independently configured log handlers, then verify secrecy and retained diagnostic utility at each boundary.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure that secrets embedded in exception diagnostics or log records cannot cross the affected consumer-facing diagnostic boundaries while structured errors and useful non-secret context remain intact.
when_to_use: A structured error result exposes raw exception messages, tracebacks, command context, or comparable diagnostic text to an external consumer.
A subsystem replaces inherited logging handlers or formatters and therefore bypasses an established application-wide redaction formatter.
An existing, tested sensitive-text redaction policy can be reused at the emission boundary.
anti_goals: Do not remove the error result, traceback field, log destination, log layout, filters, or status information merely to avoid leakage.
Do not redesign or broaden the secret-detection algorithm when the demonstrated defect is an emission boundary that fails to invoke the existing policy.
Do not claim closure of unrelated secret-emission gaps outside the inspected exception-result and ACP stderr surfaces.
not_applicable_when: The diagnostic text is already demonstrably redacted after all formatting and immediately before emission.
No trusted redaction function or formatter exists and its detection behavior cannot be established from implementation and tests.
The data must remain byte-exact for an authorized internal-only consumer and applying this redactor would violate that explicit contract.
inputs: Inventory of externally visible diagnostic-result fields and independently configured log handlers
Existing sensitive-text redaction function and redacting log formatter
Representative secret-bearing exceptions and log records
Branch controls needed to reach each affected exception path
Test runner capable of executing the focused regression tests
workflow_graph.entry_state: At least one externally observable diagnostic path emits exception-derived or log-formatted text without applying the shared redaction policy at its final boundary.
workflow_graph.exit_state: All evidenced diagnostic paths apply the shared redaction policy immediately before structured serialization or during final log formatting, and focused tests demonstrate that raw secrets are absent while response structure and useful context are retained.

steps.condition: Required for each structured exception-result branch that can contain exception-derived secret material.
steps.validation: Exercise the generic and configured degraded-fail branches; verify the secret is absent from error and traceback while status and useful failure context remain.

steps.condition: Required when the subsystem clears or replaces inherited handlers and assigns its own formatter.
steps.validation: Format a secret-bearing record through the installed handler; verify the raw value is absent and the non-secret key label remains.

validation_ladder: Static comparison: confirm each raw emission point in the parent is replaced by the shared redaction function or formatter without changing unrelated routing and response structure.
Branch-level structured-result tests: inject a secret-bearing generic exception and a degraded-fail connection exception, then inspect every returned diagnostic field.
Sink-level logging test: format a secret-bearing record through the exact handler installed by subsystem logging setup.
Integration check: run the three focused regression tests together in an environment with the repository's test dependencies.
Broader regression check: run the surrounding terminal-tool, ACP-adapter, and redaction test suites to detect formatting, filtering, or response-contract regressions.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the parent and after states do not identify a concrete unredacted emission boundary.
Stop if redaction is applied only to an internal logger copy while another consumer-facing copy remains raw.
Stop if the focused tests do not assert both secret absence and preservation of the required diagnostic contract.
Do not report runtime validation as passed when the test runner or dependencies are unavailable.
unresolved_or_deferred: Focused runtime tests were not executed during extraction because pytest is unavailable in the supplied environment.

The commit explicitly states that process-list output, additional environment-key variants, and control-character-split tokens were handled by separate changes; their implementation and validation are outside this episode.
The workflow contains two independently required branches with no evidence-backed ordering dependency between them; completion requires validating both when both boundary types are present.

unresolved_questions: Do the three focused tests pass at the pinned commit under the repository's supported dependency environment? Runtime execution was unavailable locally because pytest is not installed.
Do broader terminal-tool, ACP-adapter, and redaction suites reveal compatibility regressions? The available evidence contains focused tests but no GitHub status-check or review metadata.
The issue bundle lacks the issue/PR body, comments, reviews, timeline, and status checks, so no claims are made about reviewer intent or CI results beyond the commit and checked-in tests.
